answer: Each identity claims one ledge plot and posts a 75-credit bond. It runs a sable thread along three baselines and files signed angle readings with the haven registry. An auditor recomputes the triangle: angles must sum to 180 and match baseline lengths, or the bond burns. Fees rise per baseline reuse: the first pays 33 credits, the kth pays 33+8(k-1), so the 1000th pays 8025 and 1,000 fakes pay 4,029,000 in fees plus 75,000 locked. An honest surveyor pays 33 once and keeps the bond after one clean epoch. A rented-survey ring fails: one angle set cannot fit two keys, so reuse burns both bonds.
